scenes.title: SQL Clauses
scenes.narration: Clauses are the modular parts of a query, and each one refines the result in a predictable way.

scenes.title: Common clauses
bullets: ORDER BY sorts the final output
scenes.narration: FROM tells the query which table to read from, forming the foundation of the result. WHERE then filters that data so only rows meeting your condition remain. ORDER BY arranges the surviving rows into the sequence you want to see.

scenes.title: Logical clause order
scenes.narration: The database evaluates clauses in a logical order, not the order you type them. It starts with FROM and WHERE to gather and filter rows, then groups and filters groups with GROUP BY and HAVING. SELECT and ORDER BY come last, which is why an alias made in SELECT cannot be used in WHERE.

scenes.title: Clauses working together
scenes.code:
SELECT department, COUNT(*)
FROM employees
WHERE active = true
GROUP BY department
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC;
scenes.narration: FROM reads the employees table and WHERE keeps only active staff. GROUP BY then collapses the rows into one per department, and COUNT tallies each group. Finally ORDER BY sorts the departments from largest headcount to smallest.

scenes.text: Understanding the logical order of clauses explains why queries behave the way they do.
scenes.narration: Knowing the logical order in which clauses run explains many surprising query behaviors and helps you build them correctly.
